_comment: The strategic-AI migration domain (RI-AI). This profile is a LIFT, not a redesign: every
value here was a hardcoded constant in gen_migration.py / migration_ready.py / migration_session.py /
migration_loop.py before 2026-08-07, and the acceptance test for the lift was that regenerating the
manifest through the profile reproduces tools/data/ai_migration.json byte-for-byte.
Do not 'tidy' a value here without regenerating and diffing the manifest.
title: Strategic AI

root.name: llm_strat_ai_players_tick
root.why: VERIFIED (docs/ai-closure.md): llm_strat_sim_step has 14 direct callees and exactly one is AI, so this is the sole entry into the AI from the sim tick.

select.why: The cluster was already named consistently, so the prefix IS the membership test. Note this is right for deciding what to REWRITE and wrong for deciding what a translation TOUCHES -- the callee frontier is derived from the call graph instead (migration_ready.py's R2).

owned_elsewhere.name: llm_strat_ai_group_move_formation_rotating
owned_elsewhere.why: RE-HOMED 2026-08-28 (O4B). It carries the llm_strat_ai_ prefix and nothing else about it is AI: its whole body stamps units[p][id].order_notify_status = 1 and .order_status_flags |= 0x40, calls llm_strat_unit_order_move_enqueue once per harvested member, and bumps _G_LLM_STRAT_ORDER_SEQ_ID_BY_PLAYER (skipping 0 on wrap). Those two fields MEASURE as sim-written / AI-read order-pipeline state, not AI state -- llm_strat_unit_notify_status writes both at six sites (sim_unit_notify.cpp), sim_target_release_ref and sim_storage_scrap write order_status_flags, and the only AI touches are READS (ai_group_task_predicates.cpp's readiness switch, ai_group_move_helpers.cpp's 0x80 test). So the write is an order-issue write, and homing it here would have needed a mutable `units` in ai_store -- the R2 hole ai_state.h names in as many words. The orders_issue domain already owns exactly this shape.

owned_elsewhere.name: llm_strat_ai_unit_flag_and_move
owned_elsewhere.why: RE-HOMED 2026-08-28, on the same measurement that settled llm_strat_ai_group_move_formation_rotating in O4B and with the same verdict: behaviour owns the function, the llm_strat_ai_ prefix does not. Both bodies write EXACTLY the two order-pipeline fields that one writes, at the same offsets with the same constants -- units[p][id].order_notify_status = 1 (unit +0xe8) and .order_status_flags |= 0x40 (unit +0xe3) -- and then call llm_strat_unit_order_move_enqueue. Those two fields measure as sim-written / AI-READ order-pipeline state (llm_strat_unit_notify_status writes both at six sites in sim_unit_notify.cpp; the AI only reads them), so the write is an order-issue write. llm_strat_ai_unit_flag_and_move is 73 bytes and is NOTHING BUT that stamp plus the enqueue -- ten AI group tasks call it as their move primitive. llm_strat_ai_group_scatter_to_passable_tile is the same stamp behind a passable-tile pick. Homing either in `ai` would have needed a mutable `units` in ai_store for a body that only stamps order bits -- the R2 hole ai_state.h names in as many words, and exactly what O4B's re-home avoided. The eight roster writers that remain in batch D are a different case and DO stay in `ai`: they write ai_group_next/_prev/_index and player_data.ai_groups[], which is the AI's own linked list living inside the sim's frozen record layout.

roster_batch.why: writes the sim roster(s) %s -- the AI's own state living inside the sim's frozen record layout, translated under AI1D
roster_batch._why_it_is_a_translation_batch_now: CHANGED 2026-08-28 (user's call). Batch D used to be `refactor_batch` -- not a translation batch at all, but AI2's R2 burn-down, which planned to convert these writers into ORDER EMITTERS. That is why AI2 could not coexist with AI1-P's bit-identity clause, and why AI1's done_when quantified over A/B/C/E only and left ten functions permanently `not_started`. D1 (docs/state-boundary.md) froze the state LAYOUT after AI2 was written, and that changes the answer: under a frozen layout these are ordinary functions that write bytes at fixed offsets, and translating them bit-identically is an ordinary migration -- the same move SIM-RESID made for the scripted event drivers. AI2 survives as the LATER refactor, and gets easier: it rewrites bodies we own instead of original code. MEASURED before the move: the ten split 4/6, and two of the four were not AI at all (see select.owned_elsewhere).

unreachable_batch.why: not reachable from players_tick -- fires on another clock, needs a caller-side hook

region_hints_why: R6's zero-size-region filter. The pre-profile code was `"_AI_" in name OR name.startswith("AI")`; both arms match zero regions today, and both are covered by these two substrings. A BARE "AI" would be wrong -- it matches MAIN.

rig._why: The AI cluster's sites hang off llm_strat_ai_players_tick, which a single-AI loadgame run reaches at a controlled step -- so `sp` is the cheaper vehicle and the default. `soak` (the all-AI self-playing match) reaches the same sites and is kept for the cross-check, not because a second one is needed.

refactor_why: RETIRED as a batch mapping 2026-08-28: batch D is now a TRANSLATION batch (AI1D) and AI2 is the later order-emitter refactor layered on the translated bodies. Kept as a note because the reason batch D existed at all -- these functions write the sim rosters -- is still true and is still what makes them the interesting batch.

items._interface_why: The tracker item that OWNS building the state interface this domain's batches translate into -- `<D>0` in the reimpl-decompose skill's vocabulary, and the item it calls the highest-leverage one. Declared here rather than derived from the domain name because orders_issue's is `O4-0` and a future domain may reuse another domain's interface outright. tools/lint_migration_items.py checks it exists, is not an orphan, and is REACHABLE THROUGH DEPS from every batch. The const AI state view + `libmh_selftest.exe aitest`. Batch A deps on it directly; B/C/E chain through A.
